title: Don Byas back in New York with a bayonet: 'I am him'
summary: Both Byas and Butler were afraid to leave their rooms after returning from France; Byas carried a French bayonet, turned religious, and scattered thieves in Beefsteak Charlie's.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: See, coming back to New York is an awful thing

after you been away a long time.
You see all the decay and you are fighting -- you see these characters standing on these corners, you know they don't have a good will message for you, and you are accustomed to quietness and courtesy, all these things -- so Don, he went to a hotel on 8th Avenue and stayed in there for two weeks, scared to come out.

I did the same thing, when I come back. I was afraid to come out. I didn't come out. And Don, he says, I can't -- I don't understand what's going on, so then he stayed in the house for two weeks and then went somewhere and bought a bayonet -- one of those French bayonets --
It's a bayonet, yeah, it's a bayonet, you know, like you put on --

And he had this French bayonet, and it's a very long thing, it's got three prongs on it, he had this walking around and he became very vindictive, because that's his nature. He became very vindictive.
Then he, I met him in a place called Beefsteak

Charlie's and Don was so frantic, I said, well, Don, come on, let me buy you something to drink. No, don't want nothing. Because he was accustomed to drinking that Bull's gin in Harlem, and he was drinking the -- straight -- and then he became ultra-religious.
And then he said -- All these people talking about God, but you don't know where at, where he's at. I am him -- ' and all the thieves ran. Everybody ran.
When he made that statement all them old thieves, muggers, in Beefsteak Charlie's---they cut out.
Left him there. And I was at the end of the bar, I'm watching a few order up some more -- I was gone. That's the last time I saw my man. That's what happened.
